observations.canvasAnchor: ō# is never translated literally as ‘already.’
In a mainline reflexive-object construction, subposition va1 carries person information.
+M-o( ~ +m-⎕( is the nonfirst-person reflexive-object morphic alternation.
The contrast between tē and tla is not a contrast of animateness.
The customary-present tense morph is ni.
Person is never the only information manifested in subposition va1.
The morph itz is subject to assimilation.
The plural-number carrier in has ih as a subvariant.
The morph am occurs before m.
When a mainline reflexive object precedes a verbstem whose initial [i] is merely supportive, that supportive [i] is no longer needed and is omitted.
Omission of supportive [i] after a reflexive object is a positive phonological realization, not evidence that the stem or result is absent.
Tla fusion is a derivational process.
A surface form containing tla may instead instantiate a derived intransitive stem created by tla fusion.
this is indicated in writing by replacing a period with a question mark.
The second-person-singular Class B admonition of (huetzi) is realized as mā tihuetz with singular num² shape ⎕-Ø.
Mā gives the proposition wish or optative force.
Mā marks Mā nihcihui as a nonpast optative exhortation.
In the grammar's analytical spelling of negative wishes, prefixal ca# is attached to the VNC it negates.
The /e:/ before the glottal stop in huē-hue-h is shortened.
furthermore, its perfective stem is used to form VNCs in only the preterit-as-present tense.
Active projective object c-Ø is promoted to common-number subject Ø-Ø+…+Ø-Ø in the passive transform.
After the mainline reflexive-object pronoun is converted into the passive subject, shuntline ne persists as a representative of its reflexive nature.
The chart contains exactly thirteen three-pronoun combinations licensed by the ordering rules.
Type-two applicative verbstems are more frequent than type-one applicatives and are formed with the suffixal units liā and huiā.
The ti morph occurs after a vowel.
